title: Evaluating AI Search: A Practical Framework for Augmented AI Systems — Quotient AI + Tavily
talk_summary: Quotient AI and Tavily describe how to evaluate AI search/retrieval systems: static benchmarks like SimpleQA mislead because the web changes and rankings shift, so they generate dynamic, evidence-grounded eval sets from multiple search providers and use reference-free metrics (answer completeness, document relevance, hallucination detection) to diagnose failures without ground truth. The core transferable idea is a diagnostic eval loop that tells you which failure mode occurred and what to fix, not just a score.

takeaways.technique: Reference-free diagnostic metrics instead of single pass/fail score
takeaways.what_they_do: Score each response on answer completeness, document relevance, and hallucination rate, then combine them to infer the failure type and the fix (e.g., incomplete + relevant docs + no hallucination => retrieve more documents).
takeaways.evidence_quote: your evaluation should do more than just provide relative rankings. It should help you identify the types of issues that are present
takeaways.numbers: answer completeness correlated 0.94 with reference-based average performance

takeaways.what_they_do: An open-source LangGraph agent generates domain-targeted queries, pulls grounding documents from multiple search providers (not just their own, to reduce bias), and generates QA pairs that must cite the evidence used.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use multiple real-time AI search providers to both maximize coverage and minimize bias

takeaways.technique: Require grounding evidence for every judgment
takeaways.what_they_do: The generation agent is obliged to emit the answer context/evidence for each QA pair so outputs are auditable and hallucination is reduced.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent is obliged to to generate answer context which al which also increase the reliability of our question and answer pairs

takeaways.technique: Demand retrieved documents, not just citations, from tools
takeaways.what_they_do: They note most search providers return only citations, which blocks relevance/hallucination scoring; only providers returning retrieved documents can be debugged at scale.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the majority of search providers typically only provide citations and these are largely unhelpful at scale
takeaways.numbers: only 3 of the search providers returned retrieved documents

takeaways.technique: Track eval runs over time with an observability tool
takeaways.what_they_do: They log offline eval runs in LangSmith to compare performance across time steps and detect regressions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use length miss to track our experiments which is a great observability tool to manage these uh offline um evaluation runs
